title: Existence of winning tickets in noisy textual domains and improved generalization at moderate sparsity
content: A binary sentiment analysis task on five Amazon Reviews domains (Books, Electronics, Movies, CDs, Home) using a CNN with three filter heights $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, each with 127 channels, ReLU activation, 1-max pooling, one hidden MLP layer of dimension 117, embedding dimension $d=417$, max sequence length $n=500$, embeddings initialized from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ and convolutional/MLP layers initialized with He initialization (weights uniformly sampled from $\mathcal{U}(-b,b)$ where $b=\sqrt{\frac{6}{(1+a^2)\times\text{fan\_in}}}$ with $a$ and $\text{fan\_in}$ being per-weight parameters), trained with Adam at learning rate $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$, and iterative magnitude pruning with layerwise magnitude selection (prune fraction $p=35\%$ per round, total rounds $r_{total}=20$, yielding sparsity $1-(1-0.35)^{20}$) produces sparse subnetworks (tickets) that, when reinitialized to their original initial values (TICKET-RESET) and retrained in isolation, achieve test accuracy comparable to or better than the unpruned full model (FULL-MODEL) for moderate sparsity levels, with TICKET-RESET outperforming FULL-MODEL in the early-to-moderate sparsification regime (approximately 0%–90% sparsity) for the Books, Electronics, and Home domains.

title: Random re-initialization performs comparably to original initialization up to high sparsity (~96%)
content: On the five Amazon Reviews domains (Books, Electronics, Movies, CDs, Home) with a CNN architecture (three filter heights $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, each with 127 channels, ReLU activation, 1-max pooling, one hidden MLP layer of dimension 117, embedding dimension $d=417$, max sequence length $n=500$, embeddings initialized from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ and convolutional/MLP layers initialized by He initialization with weights uniformly sampled from $\mathcal{U}(-b,b)$ where $b=\sqrt{6/((1+a^2)\times\text{fan\_in})}$ with $a$ and $\text{fan\_in}$ per-weight parameters) trained with Adam at learning rate $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$, and iterative magnitude pruning (prune fraction $p=35\%$ per round, $r_{total}=20$ rounds), resetting the retained weights of a sparse subnetwork to random draws from the original initialization distributions (TICKET-RANDOM) yields test performance statistically similar to resetting to the original initial values (TICKET-RESET) for sparsity levels up to approximately $96\%$. Specifically, for sparsities below $96\%$, the mean test accuracies and standard deviations of TICKET-RANDOM and TICKET-RESET overlap closely across all evaluated domains.

title: Phase transition at approximately 96% sparsity where original initialization yields greater stability and accuracy
content: Using the five Amazon Reviews domains (Books, Electronics, Movies, CDs, Home) and the CNN architecture (three filter heights $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, 127 channels, ReLU, 1-max pooling, MLP dim 117, embedding dim 417, max seq length 500, embeddings from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, conv/MLP He initialization (weights from $\mathcal{U}(-b,b)$ with $b=\sqrt{6/((1+a^2)\times\text{fan\_in})}$), Adam lr $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$) with iterative magnitude pruning ($p=35\%$, $r_{total}=20$), a phase transition occurs at approximately $96\%$ sparsity: beyond this threshold, subnetworks reinitialized to random draws from the original initialization distributions (TICKET-RANDOM) exhibit rapid test accuracy degradation and high instability, whereas subnetworks reinitialized to their original initial values (TICKET-RESET) maintain substantially better and more stable test accuracy, even at sparsity levels exceeding $99.9\%$. Thus, the choice of initialization is largely immaterial below approximately $96\%$ sparsity but becomes crucial for preserving accuracy and reducing variance in the extreme-sparsity regime.

title: Sparse masks transfer across distinct text domains with modest accuracy loss up to high sparsity (≈90%)
content: Under the iterative magnitude pruning procedure (prune fraction $p=35\%$, $r_{total}=20$) with the CNN architecture and training details (five Amazon Reviews domains, CNN with filters $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, 127 channels, ReLU, 1-max pooling, MLP dim 117, embedding dim 417, max seq length 500, embeddings from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, conv/MLP He initialization (weights from $\mathcal{U}(-b,b)$ with $b=\sqrt{6/((1+a^2)\times\text{fan\_in})}$), Adam lr $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$), when sparse masks $m$ obtained from a source domain $\mathcal{D}_s$ are applied to a target domain $\mathcal{D}_t$ (with $\mathcal{D}_s \neq \mathcal{D}_t$) and the retained parameters are reinitialized either to the source-domain original values (MASKS-RESET) or to random draws from the original initialization distributions (MASKS-RANDOM), the resulting subnetworks retrain in the target domain with only modest accuracy degradation relative to tickets obtained directly in the target domain via the same procedure (TICKET-TARGET) for sparsity levels up to approximately $90\%$. Quantitatively, for transfers from Books and Electronics source domains, the test-accuracy dropoff is roughly $3–5\%$ (absolute) up to $\sim90\%$ sparsity; overall, both MASKS-RESET and MASKS-RANDOM maintain relatively stable accuracies from 0% to 90% sparsity and decline more significantly only beyond this range.

title: Domain-specific exceptional robustness: CDs-derived masks outperform target-domain tickets even at extreme sparsity
content: Across the five Amazon review domains (Books, Electronics, Movies, CDs, Home) under the lottery ticket transfer procedure (iterative magnitude pruning with $p=35\%$, $r_{total}=20$, CNN architecture with $h\in\{3,4,5\}$, 127 channels, ReLU, 1-max pooling, MLP dim 117, embedding dim 417, max seq length 500, embeddings from $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$, conv/MLP He initialization, Adam lr $1\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $\ell_2$ weight $1\mathrm{e}{-5}$, batch size 32, dropout $p=0.285$), masks obtained from the CDs domain and applied to any other target domain (with MASKS-RESET or MASKS-RANDOM) outperform the subnetworks obtained directly in that target domain (TICKET-TARGET) and retain stronger performance even at sparsity levels exceeding $99\%$.
